data.gender_notes: Aleris is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek element 'aleros' meaning 'other' or 'different'. In mythology, Aleris was a name for the goddess Hera in the form of a watchful or protective deity. This name carries the essence of being otherworldly and alert, as well as having a noble and watchful nature. The name Aleris carries the meaning “Other alert, watchful, or noble” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Aleris usually hope their child will grow to embody other alert, watchful, or noble and live with faith, good character and purpose.

In later years, it became popular in the Middle Ages, particularly in England, and was often given to children born out of wedlock, symbolizing a different and unique identity.
data.spiritual_significance: Aleris can signify a strong and vigilant spirit, one that watches over and protects. It can represent the internal voice that guides us and reminds us of our unique identity and purpose in life, encouraging us to stand out and be different in a positive way. Additionally, this name can also be seen as a reminder of the watchful and nurturing presence of the Divine, particularly in the form of the Virgin Mary who watches over and protects her children.
